flags: FHWA gives the designated byway as 27 miles; material gives a shorter mapped distance. Woodward Avenue, M-1 and the heritage corridor are not identical. The southernmost avenue block is pedestrian; M-1 ends before Pontiac.
Cache 01 is a Wayback navigation shell, not the archived MDOT PDF. It supports no designation claims. Federal designation and heritage description use FHWA cache 30.

Cache 31 says 12,000 Model Ts were built at Piquette; cache 32 says 14,000 U.S.-built cars. Omitted the production total. Moving-line experiments here used a Model N; formal moving assembly production belongs to Highland Park.

Moments run south to north, reversing the material strip-mile direction. The Dream Cruise is a corridor-wide annual event, placed after 6–7 Mile at its Ferndale beginning, not a permanent roadside display. No current event access or traffic-management claim is made.

The concrete milestone is supported only by Wikipedia in this cache. The text does not claim the original 1909 pavement survives. The road’s Indigenous predecessor is named without assigning an unsupported nation.
Preserved the story-level steeple-town motif: cache 31 documents Piety Hill and 22 National Register churches, though the narrative focuses on automobile history.
